learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected $5 against $1 and $3 minimum worthwhile offer under money-only whole-dollar model; locked it in.
observations.exploration: Tested $5: accept gives5/5, reject0/0. $1: accept1/9, reject0/0, accept beats0. $0: accept0/10, reject0/0; own payoff equal, nothing to gain. Values observed directly in screenshots; AX names diagram but omits payoff contents.
observations.reveal: Corrected $1; explained positive payoff versus0 and indifference at0. Rejection costs self1 and proposer9. Derived proposer offers1 if knows money-only responder. Explicitly says fairness preference can justify rejection under different model.
observations.visual: Actual1257 ×936 dark screenshots inspected at5,1,0 and reveal. Coin split,paired outcome boxes and dashed indifference boxes show own/proposer payoffs. Full reveal legible.

prediction.reason: Clear commitment tests fair-split intuition against explicit monetary objective.

interaction.reason: Positive offers and zero boundary expose accept/reject monetary comparison.

payoff.reason: Connects tested $1 and $0 to threshold and explicitly limits money-only assumption.

clarity.reason: Outcome boxes and own/proposer labels clarify tested visual path.

transfer.reason: Concrete proposer application with knowledge and preference conditions explained.
transfer.evidence: Proposer who knows money-only responder offers1; fairness changes model.

accessibility.reason: No sufficient access audit; diagram payoff values not in observed AX tree.
accessibility.evidence: Screenshot used for values; other access modes untested.

surprise.reason: Fair-minimum prediction contradicted under stated money-only objective,which strongly cues answer.

visualExplanation.reason: Split coins and paired outcome boxes carry payoff comparison.
visualExplanation.evidence: Solid accept advantage versus dashed equal-zero boxes.

playfulness.reason: Offer presets permit reversible comparison but no actual accept/reject choice.

practicalValue.reason: Concrete distinction between monetary objective and fairness preference.
practicalValue.evidence: Model explicitly changes when fairness matters.

depth.reason: Positive incentive,zero boundary and proposer response linked.

complexity.reason: Separates self-payoff from fairness and adds conditional proposer reasoning.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Compare two-player outcomes under fixed preference,then infer proposer response.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low for tested visual path: presets and two payoff boxes.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: ultimatum-game incentive and preference assumption.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: low: dollar payoffs and ten coins.

whyCool: At zero both own-payoff boxes become equal,while at one dollar accepting still visibly beats rejecting.
caveat: No real responder behavior or fairness utility tested; accept/reject boxes are displayed comparisons rather than active choices.
missingEvidence: $3 and slider endpoint beyond presets not tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
